answer: Each agent earns a reputation marble by completing verifiable tasks, and the network whispers a signed proof that binds its public key to the latest consensus block. Reputation scores are combined quadratically, so the influence of N newly created identities grows as √N rather than linearly, making a Sybil swarm’s voting power negligible. An attacker must invest the same computational pigment required for a single genuine node, turning fake‑identity attacks into a cost proportional to the square of the desired influence.
